newsitem.title: INDIA: India appoints chief telecom regulator.
newsitem.headline: India appoints chief telecom regulator.

text.p: The Indian government on Wednesday appointed S.S. Sodhi, a former High Court chief judge, as the first chairman of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Sodhi has been appointed for a five-year term, the news agency said.
The TRAI will regulate the telecommunications industry, particularly basic telephone services, which India opened up to the private sector under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.

The regulator is expected to resolve disputes between telephone service companies, ensure technical compatibility and inter-connectivity between them, regulate tariffs and protect consumer interests and competition.

The TRAI has been set up by a presidential decree, and must be replaced by a law. A bill is expected to be introduced in the budget session of parliament beginning on Thursday to replace the presidential ordinance by a law.
